data.name: WebEventFlowBlock_SpecialExplanation_BestPractice_LinkExtractionAndSwitch
data.value:
Best practice: extract links, then open links.$$CONTINUE$$ - Web-Selector: collect target href values. - Web-Event (Switch to URL): iterate collected URLs. - Then run detail/download actions on the opened page.
Benefit: - Iteration is based on stable URL values (not DOM element handles). - This avoids stale-element issues after navigation/re-render.

data.name: WebEventFlowBlock_SpecialExplanation_EventType_ClickAll
data.value: Hints for event: ClickAll$$CONTINUE$$ - Executes all matching clicks in sequence. - Does not create a separate result iteration for each clicked element. - Writes one DOM result only after all clicks have finished.

data.name: WebEventFlowBlock_SpecialExplanation_EventType_UpdateDOM
data.value: Hints for event: UpdateDOM$$CONTINUE$$ - Replaces the DOM content of the element resolved by XPath or CSS selector. - Uses the input text as the new DOM content. - This is intended for controlled DOM manipulation before subsequent web actions or selectors run.

data.name: WebEventFlowBlock_SpecialExplanation_BestPractice_MultiPageLinkExtraction
data.value:
Best practice for links across multiple pages: - Step 1: Web-Event (search/submit) -> Web-Selector (collect target links) - Step 2: From the paging path, use a Web-Selector to check for the next-page element -> Web-Event (click next page) - Step 3: Web-Event (click next page) -> Injection back to the search/submit result flow block; map the current DOM content to its result field. Injection then resumes at the target's successors.$$CONTINUE$$
Repeat until no next-page element is available.
Do/Don't: - Do: route Injection back to the result flow block at the paging entry (for example the search/submit Web-Event). - Don't: use Recursive call when search/submit must not execute again. It actually executes the target flow block again. - Don't: target data-record selectors or iterators with Injection, because they produce data-record output rather than paging state. - Do: run next-page selector/click from the paging element path (once per page). - Don't: place next-page selector/click behind the data-iteration block, otherwise paging runs per record instead of per page.
If a Join collector should aggregate links across all page iterations: - Set Join.AssociatedIterationContext to the predecessor of the paging WebEvent (Web-Event: search/submit). - Then aggregation runs after the full paging scope.

data.name: RecursiveCallFlowBlock_SpecialExplanation_TargetInvocation
data.value:
The target flow block itself is executed again, followed by its regular execution path. No fields are transferred. The target must already lie on the incoming execution path.$$CONTINUE$$
Example of a delayed retry: - Execute a database query and check its result. - If no result is available: execute Index and check whether Index < RetryLimit. Only then execute Delay -> Recursive call with the database query as its target. - As soon as a result is available, continue along the regular success branch.
Set AssociatedContextualObject of the Index flow block to the flow block immediately before the target, for example the database query's predecessor. This resets the counter for a new input context while continuing to count recursive attempts within that context. Once RetryLimit is reached, the retry condition is no longer satisfied; Delay and Recursive call are not executed and no further recursive iteration is created.
